summary: Iter13 — fully verified end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest passing (/app/backend/tests/test_iter13.py) covering POST /api/network/profile (with/without password, empty SSID->400, lowercase security auto-uppercased to WPA3, label preserved, has_password reflects body, password & password_hash NEVER returned), GET /api/network/profiles (most-recent-first, no password/password_hash leakage), DELETE /api/network/profile/{id} (deletes profile + matching WIFI:<ssid[:16]> peripheral_link, 404 on unknown id), network/graph picks up new WIFI:<ssid> peripheral node, [NETWORK-PROFILE] memory written with tags ['wifi','profile','<security_lower>'], regression on /api/bridge/web, /api/introspect, /api/lattice/nodes. Frontend: [data-testid=center-tab-connect] is the 4th tab after NEURAL/OBSERVE/NETWORK; ConnectScreen renders network-telemetry, device-pair (3 pair-* buttons), wifi-manifest (ssid/password/security/label inputs + connect-btn). Filling SSID='Althea-Lab', WPA3, password='sovereign', label='lab1' + clicking wifi-connect-btn cleared all inputs, fired POST /api/network/profile (body confirmed contained ssid+security+password+label), and listed the profile [data-testid=wifi-profile-<uuid>] with its delete button. Clicking delete fired DELETE /api/network/profile/<id> and removed the row. Spawned a cognitive node via /spawn iter13_x, then triggered a bridge fetch to example.com from NETWORK; both COG (network-node-cog:NODE-0000) and HOST (network-node-host:example.com) appear in graph. Clicking inner picking-circle of cog node opens [data-testid=memory-drawer] with [data-testid=memory-search-input] pre-populated to 'NODE-0000' (exact match). Clicking host node does NOT open the drawer and DOES fire POST /api/bridge/web AND shows the in-NetworkScreen bridge result panel ([data-testid=bridge-result-dismiss] visible) with HOST hover detail visible. No console errors (only benign WebGL ReadPixels + THREE.Clock deprecation warnings).

issues: The <g data-testid=network-node-...> bounding box includes the label text to the right of the circle, so the bbox center sits on the text (which has pointerEvents:none). Real users still hit the visible glowing dot, but automation using locator.click()/bbox-center misses it. The picking circle (transparent r=max(r+4,10)) is small. Consider enlarging picking circle to r=14-16 OR moving labels under the circle so bbox center aligns with the clickable spot — would also help touch users.

action_items: (Optional UX) Enlarge the picking circle in NetworkScreen from max(r+4,10) to ~14-16 OR shift label text below/above the circle so the SVG <g> bbox centers on the clickable disc. Pure UX/automation polish — functionality is correct.
(Optional) ConnectScreen sends password:null when empty — backend treats falsy as 'open', which is correct, but consider omitting the field entirely from the JSON for cleanliness.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/web_bridge.py:264 — SHA-256 with no salt is acceptable here because the value is never used for authentication (no compare path), just an integrity hash for the manifest. Document this intent in a comment so a future dev doesn't think it's password verification.

backend/routers/web_bridge.py:265 — upsert by ssid means re-saving the same SSID UPDATES (not creates) and reuses the same id only if upsert matched; the new model_dump generates a fresh uuid each call but the $set will overwrite the doc's id field. This means re-submitting the same SSID rotates the id but POST returns the in-memory profile.id (which is the new one). Verify by GET /profiles whether DB id matches returned id after a re-submit of an existing ssid. Suggest: on conflict, return the existing doc's id (find_one first, then upsert with that id) OR use ssid as the unique key.
frontend ConnectScreen.jsx — pair* buttons will fail in headless playwright (no real device dialog); confirmed acceptable per request. Failures are caught and displayed in red, good.
NetworkScreen.jsx click handler is inline inside .map(); fine for n<200 nodes but consider useCallback if graph grows.
ConnectScreen profile list lacks a polling interval — relies on user-triggered loadProfiles. Acceptable since user is the only mutator of this list from this client.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all required iter13 acceptance criteria

seed_data_creation: Test profiles prefixed TEST_ (TEST_Althea-Lab, TEST_OpenLab, TEST_DeleteMe) were created and then cleaned up by test_zz_cleanup. UI test created an 'Althea-Lab' profile and deleted it within the same run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter13 backend regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_iter13.py. To verify SVG node clicks in playwright, query the inner <circle> via JS and click its getBoundingClientRect center — bbox of <g> includes label text and misses the hotspot. POST/DELETE network/profile fully verified incl. peripheral_link + memory side-effects. The wifi 'connect' button is intentionally a profile-declaration only (browsers cannot join wifi); banner in UI communicates this honestly.
rca of the issue: Initial automation false-fail on cog/host click was a SELECTOR issue, not a product bug: playwright's bbox-center of the <g> element lands on the label text (pointer-events:none) instead of the small transparent picking circle. Targeting the inner <circle>'s getBoundingClientRect center resolved it. Recommending a UX nudge (larger picking circle or label-below-dot) to make clicks more forgiving.
